tasks.title: Implement ngv2/semgrep_adapter.py: build_semgrep_argv + run_semgrep (injected-runner static-analysis grounding)
acceptance_criteria: New single-file module ngv2/semgrep_adapter.py exists and imports cleanly with stdlib only (no third-party imports).
build_semgrep_argv(...) deterministically constructs the semgrep command-line argument vector from its inputs (same inputs => identical argv, with stable flag/value ordering).
run_semgrep(target, *, runner) builds argv via build_semgrep_argv and reaches semgrep ONLY through the injected runner callable — no real subprocess, shell, file, or network I/O.
run_semgrep passes the build_semgrep_argv-produced argv to runner and normalizes/returns the runner's result per the oracle contract.
python -m pytest tests/test_semgrep_adapter.py -q passes against the already-committed oracle without modifying any test.
No dependency on fp_filter/confidence siblings or intake/triage/submission sub-epics; only plain imports of stable public shapes if strictly needed.

spec.objective: Provide static-analysis grounding by implementing a NEW single-file, whole-file, pure/deterministic, stdlib-only module ngv2/semgrep_adapter.py exposing build_semgrep_argv(...) and run_semgrep(target, *, runner), where semgrep is reached exclusively through the injected runner. The committed oracle tests/test_semgrep_adapter.py is the sole source of truth for exact signatures, argv shape, and runner contract.
functional_requirements: Expose build_semgrep_argv(...) that constructs the semgrep argv (e.g. base command plus config/rules, output format, target) deterministically from its inputs with stable ordering, matching the exact argv shape pinned by the oracle.
build_semgrep_argv is pure and deterministic: identical inputs yield byte-for-byte identical argv lists; no global/environment/time/randomness dependence.
Expose run_semgrep(target, *, runner) that builds the argv via build_semgrep_argv and invokes semgrep ONLY by calling the injected runner with that argv.

run_semgrep normalizes and returns the runner's result exactly as the oracle expects (preserving/translating fields per the pinned contract), performing no real subprocess/file/network I/O of its own.
Module uses stdlib only (no third-party imports) and consumes Epic-1/Epic-2 sibling modules, if at all, only via plain imports of already-tested public shapes.
Module is a single self-contained file with no cross-module wiring or integration glue beyond what the oracle requires.
spec.interfaces: ngv2/semgrep_adapter.py exposes build_semgrep_argv(...) and run_semgrep(target, *, runner). semgrep is reached only via the injected runner callable, which receives the argv produced by build_semgrep_argv. Exact parameter names, defaults, and return normalization are dictated by tests/test_semgrep_adapter.py.
edge_cases: Optional/defaulted inputs to build_semgrep_argv (e.g. config/rules, output format) must produce the deterministic argv the oracle pins.
runner that returns a non-zero/empty/error-shaped result must be normalized per the oracle rather than raising uncontrolled exceptions, if the oracle requires it.
Determinism must hold across repeated calls and across dict/iterable input ordering where the oracle requires canonicalization.
No reliance on a real semgrep binary, PATH, cwd, or environment — runner is the only boundary.
non_goals: No real subprocess, shell-out, file, or network I/O; semgrep reached exclusively via the injected runner.
Do NOT author or modify tests/test_semgrep_adapter.py or any other test/oracle.
No dependency on fp_filter/confidence siblings or on intake/triage/submission sub-epics; no cross-module wiring or integration glue.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: All verification uses the already-committed oracle tests/test_semgrep_adapter.py, which supplies fake/injected runner callables and the canonical expected argv. No new test data or fixtures are authored by this task; the listed names are descriptive references to the pinned oracle behaviors, not new tests to write.

token_budget_ratio.note: IMPL-only task: the oracle is already committed, so no new tests are authored. The test-token allocation reflects effort to read and conform to the pinned oracle (argv shape + runner contract) rather than writing new tests.
